outline: 2697 Expanding Method for Equations with Brackets

examples.solution_text:
(a) Subtract $7$ from both sides, then divide by $-4$.
$\begin{align*}7-4x&=29\\-4x&=22\\x&=-\frac{11}{2}\end{align*}$

(b) Add $6$ to both sides, then multiply by $-3$.
$\begin{align*}-6-\frac{x}{3}&=5\\-\frac{x}{3}&=11\\x&=-33\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: Solve $8-3x=23$ by first adding $3x$ to both sides.
examples.solution_text:
Add $3x$ to both sides.
$\begin{align*}8-3x&=23\\8&=23+3x\end{align*}$

Subtract $23$ from both sides, then divide by $3$.
$\begin{align*}-15&=3x\\-5&=x\end{align*}$

Subtract $15$ from both sides.
$\begin{align*}4&=15-k\\-11&=-k\end{align*}$

Since $-k=-1\times k$, divide both sides by $-1$.
$11=k$

Multiply both sides by $4$, then divide by $-3$.
$\begin{align*}-\frac{3x}{4}&=9\\-3x&=36\\x&=-12\end{align*}$

methods.description: Remove the constant from both sides, then divide by the negative coefficient, including an implicit coefficient of -1. The same operations apply when the sides are reversed.
